Review Text:
Our helicopter tour was great.

We were fortunate that the weather was about perfect; sunny, low 70s with hardly any wind.
The copter we were in had 8 seats, 4 in front and 4 in the second row. Seats are assigned (I think by weight) with 3 passengers (plus the pilot) in front and 4 passengers in the second row.
It was warm in the copter even with air conditioning.
Base on our experience it seems like the best views (although there a no bad views) are from the right side.
We appreciated the narration and explanations provided by our pilot.
We were a little surprised by the bumpiness of the ride related to the force of the chopper blades, but it is not the kind of movement that would cause motion sickness.

Our pilot (didn't catch his name) had a great sense of humour and helped us all relax so we could enjoy our flight. You don't get to choose where to sit on the helicopter as its all done by weight, but there were 3 passenger seats in the front plus the pilot and 3 seats in the back.

Review Text:
Awful experience. We had booked a 45 minute tour for myself, my daughter and my two grandsons.
When we arrived at the airfield to check in on the date and time given, we were told that the weather would not allow for the 45min flight but we could have a 25 min flight instead for a refund of $30 per person ( $30 refund on $499 for a flight only half as long!)
As we were boarding another customer started shouting hysterically that she wanted to sit in front and as we all sat there with this woman screaming, we became more and more nervous that she would lose her temper and attack the pilot once we were in flight.
Needless to say we were petrified as we took off , we flew for approx 7 minutes over trees and the helicopter was being buffeted about by the wind and it was a rough uncomfortable ride. We then reached the canyon and spent about another 7 minutes over the canyon itself again swaying and being buffeted about by the wind, and soon were on the way back for another 7 minute trip over the trees!

Thankfully the hysterical woman was silent throughout the flight but the trip I had planned as a surprise for my grandsons was an unmitigated disaster- we could not wait to get off the helicopter and leave the airfield.
How Maverick could have had the audacity to take us up in that weather is just unforgivable - it was in no way a comfortable and enjoyable experience. I have flown in several helicopters around the world- none of which were anywhere near as costly as this flight ($499 for 10 minutes over the canyon) and undertaken in such entirely unsuitable weather.

Total rip off.

PS: additionally a sticker I bought in the shop was charged at $130 when it should have been $13!!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Experience the sheer size of GC
Review Text: There’s a nice spacious area to wait and parking outside. You can’t take any baggage so leave it in your car. There’s a shop and vending machine but no coffee. The pilot was Dave, a lovely young man and experienced pilot who truly loves the GC. He gave us great information and was very friendly. You need to be weighed on arrival ( it’s discrete) and you are sat in the helicopter where they want to balance it. There are 8 seats inside with 3 in front next to the pilot and 4 behind. It isn’t bumpy and lurching - although there are a few twists and tips. It’s just exciting. It’s not like rollercoaster stunt flying, it’s very smooth really, and I was pleased I didn’t feel at all travel sick.i know it’s a costly trip, but it’s really worth it. The very best way to see some of the Grand Canyon.

Review Text:
Located at the Grand Canyon Airport which is in Tusayan Maverick Helicopters is ideally situated for sightseeing tours of the South Rim of the Grand Canyon as it takes only perhaps 5 minutes from take off to be actually in the air over the canyon. The journey to the airport from Grand Canyon Village which is where the train from Williams brought us to tak es 15 to 20 minutes by taxi and cost around $30 each way. The cab firm also stipulated payment in cash. That may change as time goes on but at the moment it seems that for them cash is the only lingua franca. After getting to the Maverick helicopter terminal we found the staff to be excellent and after checking in and weighing in too we were looked after very well until departure. The winds being rather strong and so it was decided that it was not wise to take the longer 45 minute flight that we had originally booked and we were given an option of a full refund or we could take the shorter 25 minute flight which we gladly accepted. I must say that although we missed out on the extra time and distance we still had a wonderful experience flying a mile up over the Colorado river and round the dragon in the hands of a very highly skilled pilot and in a lovely, comfortable modern helicopter. I think that whichever option suits your budget or your desire this is a great way to experience the magnificence of this wonderful place. Full marks to both the ground and air crew at Maverick.

Review Text: My Canyon Spirit  helicopter tour was part of a 2200 mile motor trip including Zion, Bryce, Monument Valley and Page.  The decision to view the Grand Canyon by air instead of hiking did not disappoint.  The weather for my 9 15 am flight was clear and calm and fellow passengers included a father/son from Germany and a senior couple from Wisconsin – all of whom were very excited for the flight.  The most amusing part of the trip was when our handsome pilot, John Paul, told us his favourite parts of the Grand Canyon after piloting the Canyon trips for a mere 5 days. As the audio briefly cut out all we heard was he had flown helicopters for 5 days !  Too funny!  (he formerly worked at the Las Vegas location)  The journey was smooth and gentle – like a flying couch – which is critical to those of us who suffer from motion sickness.  The temperature inside the helicopter was perfect – having been baked on stifling flights over Niagara Falls, Ontario, Canada and Canmore, Alberta, Canada,  I was pleased the pilot confirmed our comfort level several times.  The views are spectacular:  full of colour and texture.  Some passengers are interested in photography, others are content to soak up the views.  The richness of any experience is determined by what you bring to it – asking a few questions of the pilot who flies tourists over the Canyon every day brought a whole different perspective to the Grand Canyon experience.  For those of us not paying in US dollars its pricey but as a once in a lifetime flight it was worth it.  (And for ‘balance’ reasons I got to sit next to the pilot – it was tough but someone had to do it)

Review Text:

Review Title: The Wonder of the GC, and a great aerial photo shoot
Review Text:
My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed the ride and pilot Eddie. Very smooth ride at 7500-9500 feet which can be below the canyon rim at times. Excellent for taking aerial photos. The rear seats may be even better for photos as it has flatter plexiglass. I usually shoot open window from a plane, the plexiglass did not introduce distortion. Photos taken shutter priority 1/1000sec. f4.5, Typically 70-100mm. A wider lens 24-70mm would have been good as well. You don't need extreme telephoto.

About an hour through the ZUNI and DRAGON corridors (see GREEN route 1). Desolate territory although we saw a raft and people below.

Fantastic way to see a small part of this immense natural wonder. Both of us were very happy for the opportunity. Sights around each corner. If you use Google Earth search for KGCN for the airport.

Very professional staff, sharp looking waiting areas, utmost concern for peoples safety and comfort. Our pilot was using his checklist to go over the briefing he must have done hundreds of times to ensure he wouldn't miss anything

Review Title: Great Views Depending on Which Seats You Are Assigned
Review Text:
Maverick assigns your seats based on what other people are on the tour and weights of individual passengers. They arbitrarily combine couples or groups of passengers to each flight over the Canyon.

There are two seats in front by the pilot and there are four seats in the back. If you are fortunate enough to get the two seats in front beside the pilot or on the left rear behind the pilot, you will have amazing views. If you are assigned the two middle seats or the far right seat, forget getting to see much. The back right window is smaller and has obstructed views. Also, our pilot kept the orientation of the helicopter such that the right side was always away from the best views of the Canyon.

I would not waste my money again, since the arbitrarily seat assignment determines your views, or lack thereof.

Review Text:
The pilots are excellent, friendly, knowledgeable, and skilled.

But, don’t get your weight estimate wrong or Keith at the front desk will talk down to you as if you lied on purpose. I have family in aviation, so I understand the importance of weight distribution on an aircraft. But, when my wife’s weight came in above the number I had sent in, Keith had little to no sensitivity about it.

So, in the end my wife and I were not able to be on the same helicopter. I was upset about that, but I understand. They want to keep us safe, and flying in high heat can be dangerous. But, what I don’t appreciate is the way Keith handled the situation. Repeating statements like “This number is WAY over the estimate given to us.” is nothing short of an emotional punch in the face to anyone who has ever struggled with weight issues.

So, in the end, the stars I give are for the pilots. They are truly the 5 star champs of this company. But, my experience with Keith’s lack of sensitivity at the front desk quite literally ruined the experience for both of us. So, I would recommend that management coordinate some much needed sensitivity training for Keith. It would be a great improvement for your customer service.

Review Title: Maverick helicopter tour over Grand Canyon
Review Text: This was an amazing experience for me and my wife on our anniversary. When you fly over the forest and cross over the south rim for the first time It was awesome! You see everything, the rapids in the Colorado river, marble canyon, lava flows from Mt Humphrey and a fault line. The whole time the pilot is pointing out all of these and much more and giving some history about the Canyon as well. The tour also included the north rim as well. All the scenery just makes you go, “wow”, in awe of it all. This was my second time to the Canyon and won’t be my last. I don’t have anything I didn’t like about the tour. If you haven’t been in a helicopter you do feel some vibration but nothing excessive. There is no weightlessness feeling when taking off or landing like a plane. Maverick’s staff was very professional and provided the best service. The pilot was very professional, friendly, and knowledgeable. He made the flight more fun and interesting. I will fly again with Maverick in the future because of their customer service and staff. Thank you so much for an awesome experience!!!

Review Title: Take the Tour & Buy the Video
Review Text: Visiting the Grand Canyon National Park has been a bucket list item forever, so once we knew we were going we immediately decided on taking the Canyon Spirit helicopter tour. We are so glad we did! Flying from the south rim to the north rim was thrilling and exceeded all expectations. From the jaw dropping scenery to the excitement of it all, it was a true once-in-a lifetime experience. The staff at Maverick were very accommodating every step of the way. Our first scheduled tour had to be canceled because of bad weather. But gladly so, because safety is obviously paramount. Luckily we had one more day in the park, so we were able to reschedule our tour for the following morning, which turned out to be beautiful, rather than take the refund that was offered. Our pilot, Jesse, was awesome too, and to include very experienced, as he was a former pilot in the service. He was relaxed and personable, knowledgeable about the Grand Canyon and its surroundings, and focused on us enjoying the tour. This was our second helicopter ride (first was years ago in NYC; very cool/different), and by far our favorite between the two. The moment you first fly out over the canyon after traversing several miles over land and trees is simply breathtaking, as is when you fly over the confluence of the Colorado and Little Colorado rivers. Do not hesitate to take the tour. You will not be disappointed. And make sure to purchase the video of your tour. It’s a great keepsake.

Review Title: Just WOW - An Experience Like No Other!
Review Text: My family of 4 did this tour last week and were beyond impressed.  We opted for Maverick because of their fleet of newer helicopters with ample windows spanning down to the floor in the front.  Navigation to the airport and check in was so easy, with a relaxing space and gift shop to wait prior to the flight.  We chose the 45 minute flight because I don't know when my next opportunity will arise to take a helicopter tour, and I didn't regret this small upgrade in price.  We saw so much yet 45 minutes passed by quite quickly.  We travelled with our 7 and 10 year old children and were placed in a private tour with no others, which was wonderful and we all had a fantastic view, I was in front with the two kids and my husband was behind the pilot next to the window.  Our pilot Mark was phenomenal; very skilled in flying, knowledgeable on the geography of the Grand Canyon, and entertaining.  At no point were we nervous, even my 7 year old son, it was a very calm and amazing experience.  I was actually more nervous just walking on the trails into the canyon later that day rather than flying high over the canyon itself.  We never would have seen the Colorado River and some of the formations without taking this tour.  The only thing I would have prepped my kids with prior is that we were assigned seats once we got outside to the helicopter (they were happy and luckily we had no issues) and that once we're flying, we had to talk via the headsets.  I could tell my son started getting a little frustrated because he couldn't follow all of the pilot's information pointed out, but I was able to tell him to just relax and enjoy, there is no quiz afterwards, and he was much better after that just soaking in the sights.  You can't see the Grand Canyon like this any other way, it's such a unique experience and was well worth it.  It is an experience my family will remember forever.

Review Text:
I would highly recommend this trip to anyone considering it. The views are absolutely amazing - you wouldn't be able to see even half as much from ground level. The pilot acts as a tour guide, pointing out parts of the GC like the fault lines, the river, the Native American section etc.

Check-in process is simple and straight-forward - you need to arrive around 45 minutes in advance of the flight to check-in. There's a comfortable waiting area. You can't take any bags etc with you (you are able to take phones, cameras, water), but they check the bags in behind the front desk for you for no extra fee.

If you book through Trip Advisor they will need to see a 'payment voucher'. My email confirmation from TA sufficed.

Worth mentioning that you don't find out where you are sitting until you are there. We were lucky and ended up with front row seats. There are three front-row passenger seats, then four back-row passenger seats (two of which are window seats). I imagine this changes how much you are able to see. Our flight only had five people on it which we were told is the norm (it was peak time 12:45 in August).

Review Text: I have flown in several helicopters in various places around the world and have to say that the equipment here was top notch, one of the best I have flown. Review Text:
We flew with another outfit a few years ago and it was OK but we heard somewhere Maverick was better. It was. We paid in advance online and made an appointment. We arrived a few minutes early and were greeted cheerfully and professionally. We waited about 10 minutes and our pilot came and escorted us to the helicopter. My wife, grandson and I were joined by two other people in the 7 passenger helicopter. Pilot and three in the front, and four seat in the back. The other guy in the back and I each had a window seat with two empty seats between us. Plenty of visibility and all seats face forward. The competition has helicopters with all passenger seats in the back with half facing forward the other half facing backward.
We all had phones and my grandson had a GoPro camera so we took lots of photos and videos. Everyone had headphones and the pilot narrated the whole trip and told us the names of various features in the canyon. It was a thrilling ride and we are very pleased. We would definitely ride with Maverick again over the competition.

Review Text:
My husband and I booked the Canyon Spirit, 45-50min tour with Maverick Helicopters as part of a 3 week tour around the west of America. We booked it online a month before we went through the chat option on their website, where they gave us a bit of a discount and all the information we needed.
We were told to book in advance because it gets so busy and booked up and we were really glad we did. We did a lot of research on the different options of people to fly with and it paid off because there's nothing we'd change about the one we did. It cost $544 for both of us, which is a lot of money but we'd totally recommend it.

We flew at 8am on Thursday September 15, 2018. It was a perfect time and day. The weather was amazing and it was all perfect for the flight. You have to get there about 30 mins before the flight and you're weighed so they can allocate you in the helicopter according to weight, to spread it out. You can't choose or request a specific seat. Fortunately my husband and I got to sit in the front and it was spectacular. The helicopter is largely glass and from the front you can see right down to take in the view. However, there is a great view from every seat and I really wouldn't worry about where you sit.

Each helicopter took 6 passengers, plus the pilot.

Everyone has headphones and a microphone so you can all communicate with one another during the flight and ask questions. We were fascinated by the number of helicopters that took off at similar times but yet once you're in the air and going over the canyon you can't see any at all. It felt like you were the only one in the air and it's very difficult to take in the sheer scale of the canyon even when you can see a lot of it.

There wasn't anything scary about it or unnerving, we absolutely loved our first trip in a helicopter.

We would thoroughly recommend this trip.

Review Title: This Should be on Your Bucket List
Review Text:
A very professionally run tourist operation, and a wonderfully informed and expansive pilot who managed the dual tasks of successfully keeping us aloft while deciphering and answering our inane and long-winded questions.
And coping with our infantile exclamations.
Yes, we were excited.
All of us.
My partner and I, and the 3 other passengers - a generational trio of grandmother, mother and daughter, all on their first helicopter flight.
We had a beautiful blue sky crisp winter morning for our tour.
That moment the chopper passed from the forested plateau over the rim of the canyon was, alone, worth the cost of the flight.
My mind was then scrambled by the sheer vastness of the canyon below and around us - the northern side is evidently higher than the southern side - and the breathtaking beauty of the canyon walls and formations, the colours, the light and the shadows.
And the teal green of the serpentine Colorado way down at the very bottom.
Time evaporated as we snaked along the river, rose above then flew over the northern rim - where we saw a herd of bison in a snow covered landscape - then re-entered the canyon further westward. I couldn't believe that we had been flying for as long as we had when we gently settled back on to the tarmac back at Maverick central.
Sensational, and a video of the flight available just in case you want to relive it.

Review Title: More than i expected it to be

We travelled from Scotland to the USA to ride down the famous Route 66. One of my most anticipated stops was to see the Grand Canyon. But it was also one of my most dreaded... perhaps the hype was all just hype... what if it was an anti-climax? What if it was a complete let down...

Let me tell you it was much much more than I expected. From the ride north from Williams to the heliport, the treatment we received by Maverick Helicopters, the pilots attitude, the general experience and the Canyon itself... Wow. It wasn't a once in a lifetime, because I will go back again. And I will use Maverick Helicopters again.

Our pilot (apologies as his name escapes me... possibly Pete??), set us at ease with his relaxed but professional demeanor, his interactions with his passengers and the revelation that he used to fly Black Hawk Helicopters... so we're in good hands then. Aaaand relax. I regularly use helicopters for my work offshore, but I know my wife was incredibly nervous, and the revelation of his flying experience really helped her to enjoy the flight. It also helped to lift off to the Top Gun soundtrack, followed by a quality "mix tape" of classic rock gently pumped into our headsets as we soared over the landscape. The pilots knowledge of the area and delivery of the facts was as enjoyable as the ride itself. Outdone only by the views we experienced... I have never in all my days seen a landscape so beautiful.

Thank you Maverick Helicopters.

Jamie and Lee-Ann

Review Text:

Our pilot BJ was fabulous his manner calmed my nerves . I was extremely nervous to the point my legs were shaking , I’m a seasoned flyer but i’ve never been on a helicopter .

I was petrified ( i’m scared on kids rides at Disney! ) but knew I had to push myself as I would have regretted not taking this opportunity to see this wonder.

I was not disappointed, it was the most amazing experience of my life and I’ve been blessed to have ticked some bucket list experiences already .

Please please don’t miss out on this because of fears , you will not be disappointed .

It will give you the confidence to help overcome life’s challenges and you will look back on it and pat yourself on the back because you overcame your fears .

The ride was exciting started with rain , lightening in the distance . We were delayed slightly in the building to ensure it was safe to fly. We were kept informed and told only when safe would we go .

The initial part of the flight took us high above the forest where on our return we saw a herd of bison .

Then we waited to go over the edge , no updraft no downdraft just smooth flying and over we went , writing this my body is reminded of the nervous exhilaration I felt .

The most wonderous views of the canyon and Colorado river miles below .

Remember to stop taking pictures and video and soak up the experience through your own eyes and not a lens.

I can’t wait to do it again with my partner .

A dream come true .

Thank you BJ and Maverick 10/10

Review Title: Fly with Maverick Airlines! Fly the Canyon Dream!
Review Text: The Grand Canyon National Park is 18 miles wide and one mile deep and one of the 7 Natural Wonders of The World! I brought my 15 yr old granddaughter on the Canyon Dream trip with Maverick Airlines in their executive style, 2-pilot Beachcraft 1900 airplane, and I am really struggling to find the words to describe this amazing trip, but I have to share! First of all, the plane was airconditioned, comfortable and most of the seats have windows. The views were amazing too! When we got there, we boarded the quaint Maverick trolly that took us thru a darling little town called Tusayan, Arizona. Along the way we saw, a lot of beautiful wildlife, including the biggest Elk I've ever seen, mule deer and smaller elk! We arrived at the Maverick Helicopter terminal in a beautifully treed setting and that's where we boarded the chopper, and flew over this awe-inspiring canyon for about 20 minutes! Glorious! Stunning! Spetacular! When we got back we 'trollied' to the Bright Angel Lodge, next to the famous El Tovar Lodge where Teddy Roosavelt stayed many times in the late 1800's. We had a lunch provided by Maverick and walked around enjoying the views, got a few goodies at the gift shops, had an ice cream cone. Sat there taking it all in! A MUST SEE ~ MUST DO TRIP! Thanks to Maverick Airlines, and all the wonderful pilots and staff for the truly unforgettable Canyon Dream! By airplane, helicoper and foot!

Als Tipp: als wir in Tusayan am Vortag nachmittags ankamen, war das Wetter schlechter, es regnete, war sehr wolkig und wir dachten, unser Flug müsste ausfallen. Review Text:
We did the Canyon Dream airplane and helicopter tour in May. A truly fabulous experience with the most professional and friendly staff from start to end. Collection from our hotel and a full day of pure enjoyment (Seven hours). No photographs can project the beauty and sheer grandness of the canyon.

My sister is an extremely nervous flyer but what a supberb flying experience this was. The pilots taking us out to meet the helicopter were charming, enthusiastic and had a great sense of humour which all made for an extremely positive exerpience. The pilot invited us up to the cockpit and took photographs for us. Nothing was too much trouble and lots of interesting facts relayed throughout the plane trip.

The helicopter trip itself over the south rim of the canyon was just breathtaking. Again a great pilot, lots of chat and tremendous knowledge of the canyon.

There is also a driven tour through thre National Park taking you to scenic viewpoints to enjoy the packed lunch provided. We had a fabulous guide called Mike who was extremely knowledgeable and had a great sense of humour. It is apparent that lots of care and thought is put into Mike’s tour.

We also did the evening flight down the Las Vegas strip, breathtaking!

Can’t recommend this company highly enough. Each and every one of the people we met came across as enthusiastic, with an absolute passion to provide an unforgettable experience.

Review Text: This was by far the most breathtaking thing we did at they Grand Canyon. We hiked down 3 miles and did the entire rim, but to see so much of the canyon with such a knowledgeable guide was wonderful. We got our pictures taken in front of the chopper with the pilot before take off, and then climbed aboard the air conditioned craft. We each got a head set so we could listen to their perfectly timed background music while we asked questions or pointed out things below. We flew over the forest then  into the canyon, across both the Colorado and Little Colorado Rivers with our pilot telling us why they look different based on geology, then across the canyon to the North Rim with information on rock layers, names of peaks, information on rafting and the rapids, explorers, Native Americans, and more. We looped behind the visitor center of the North Rim (a no fly zone) and got to see wild bison below. Then back across the canyon towards the south rim for more breath taking views and over town to the airport. Our pilot was great and leaned forward out of my shot every time I pointed my camera at his window. He knew everything and was very friendly. I wish I had brought a polarized lens, as there was a bit of reflection in my pictures from the glare on the windows. My only complaint is that because they need to balance their chopper, I was not able to sit with my boyfriend for the 50 min ride, but could talk to him over the radio and did get a selfy with him behind me. My view in the front was much better than his in the back. The craft only fits 8 people, and we had 5 plus the pilot so we all got windows. I would love to do this again. Save up and go for it!

Review Title: A Once in a Lifetime - We Scored a Cracking Day!
Review Text:
Straight up, this is the single most expensive activity we did on our whole honeymoon. We debated long and hard if we could justify the cost, and researched the other operators offering similar service. We decided to go with Maverick due to their air-time and route being the most appealing we found. With all the travel we want to do around the world it is likely this would be our only visit here so we dug deep and coughed up the money as we know we'd regret if we didn't do it. We were not disappointed!

We knew there would be a few things that would have to go right for the best possible experience including the weather and our positions in the chopper. We came up trumps with both. We had a cracking day. No wind, so a smooth ride and excellent visibility. I can see people's frustration at being in the back row of the aircraft as you definitely get a better view up front and it is easier to take photos. (Though the bubble canopy makes photos without reflections tricky regardless of where you sit.) I had the good fortune of being the exact same weight as the pilot so I got a balancing seat opposite him with the little wifey sitting in the middle. The view from the back isn't terrible, but the front definitely gives the best experience. You just have to be lucky I suppose and I'm glad we were.

The Canyon was everything we hoped for and a chopper flight is easily the best way to experience it in a short period of time. We headed to the lookouts afterwards and there is simply no comparison. The pilot was skilled and the commentary informative. Every twist and turn unveiled a jaw-dropping panorama of river, rock and plateau. You spend the whole flight with a huge grin on your face and wondering if it is all real. The 45-minute flight felt sufficient and immersive, I think the shorter one would leave you wanting more. Due to the cost, I don't think I'd do it again, but you'll kick yourself if you don't do it once when you have the opportunity! It is truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience I don't think you can replicate anywhere else in the world. I thought our heli-flight back home over the Great Barrier Reef was amazing, this takes it to another level.

So no helicopter ride and robbed $600, we left the building for our first experience at the Grand Canyon Maverick Tours. I called the GM shortly after (Ted Yasuda) and got his voice recorder. I left him a detailed message, with what just happened with an optimistic spirit that somehow this would get resolved. I never received a call back from Ted Yasuda, I left several messages and still no call back, when I got back home from our Grand Canyon trip I emailed him twice, then he finally responded with an even more arrogant demeanor than his colleague Lisa Coffey. After a few email exchanges, I summarize "I will not be issuing a refund" with no apologies or attempts to bring light to a dissatisfied customer robbed of their money and experience they will never get back.

Bottom line, we planned and saved months to take our first trip to the Grand Canyon, a lifelong dream of my wife. Nothing prepared us - thankfully! - for the wonderful 45min flight over the Grand Canyon.
Professional and thorough check-in at Maverick's base, on the approach road to Grand Canyon's South Rim.
The views, the views, the views!
Like most commercial helicopter flights, our seats were allocated by our weight. No matter...we all enjoyed superb views of the Grand Canyon...I was seated in the middle of the rear row. Amazing.
The flight is just wonderful, with our pilot giving a fascinating commentary on what we were flying by and above. You can see the helicopters in front, with all aircraft following a strict, pre-determined course. So well-organised.
There was a massive choice of reasonably-priced souvenirs back at Maverick's modern base/shop, enough selection for anyone's budget.
100% I would recommend this flight if you can afford it...and even if you can't!

Review Text:
At the spur of the moment, my friend and I️ decided to take a helicopter tour of the Grand Canyon with Maverick Helicopters. While on a day tour, with Detours of Phoenix, to Sedona and the GC the option to view the canyon was offered (for an additional fee) and we jumped at the chance. Having never flown in a helicopter, and always fearful, I️ decided “I️ only live once, so why not?!”

WOW!!! What a ride! We couldn’t have asked for a better view of this beautiful natural wonder. Sean, our pilot, is professional, friendly, and reassuring. He is a former military helicopter pilot, which in my book is big deal in terms of skill (and Sean, thank you for your service). Before taking off, Sean told us about the helicopter, went over safety procedures. The ground crew assisted us in buckling up and with our headphones. Sean is quite knowledgeable of the Grand Canyon’s animal life, history and it’s many special sites, answered all our questions as we flew.

The helicopter itself is top-notch. We were told that Mavericks fleet is the youngest in the area flying the Grand Canyon. Seats are comfortable. Large viewing areas to give the best views possible. We were fortunate to have had two of the front seats, and were able to take some great shots.

The flight is 45 minutes in duration and we loved every minute of it! Thank you to Maverick and Sean for a great experience.

(A side note... I️ really enjoyed the flights playlist - Top Gun’s theme song was among some of the tunes played as we flew. Nice touch!)

Review Title: Do it, don't regret not doing so!
Review Text:
When arranging our trip to the Grand Canyon we considered the options for add ons. Ultimately the only one we organised in advance was a helicopter flight. We did so because it was our first visit to the Grand Canyon and possibly the only one given all of the other places we have on our list to visit.

Having done our research we decided on Maverick Helicopters and chose the Canyon Spirit flight. Although a little more expensive than some flights (there are shorter flights) the time in the air was approximately 45 minutes.

It was also ideal as Maverick have a base at Grand Canyon Airport, Hwy 64, Grand Canyon just 5 minutes from where we were staying at the Best Western Grand Canyon enabling us to make best use of every minute of or trip.

When first booking we were advised by our travel company that a flight time couldn't be guaranteed. Despite that we expressed a preference for an early flight to hopefully capture the views in a good light and to enable the rest of the day for other exploration of the area. Nearer our departure we made contact with Maverick and learned that weather and all else permitting our flight would be the first of the day at 08:00 am and that we needed to be there 30 minutes before. We also phoned as requested the day before our flight to check in.

We arrived early on the day at 07:20 am and checked in. We were weighed as part of the process and then waited with anticipation.

Shortly before our flight our pilot Daniel, called or name out along with the remaining passenger - 6 in total leaving one seat empty. We were escorted out onto the tarmac where we had our photographs taken by Maverick in our individual family groups with the pilot before being allocated our seats and given a safety briefing. We assume seats were allocated on the basis of balancing the weight of the group but it avoided a free for all over who would sit where.

The ECO-Star (EC130) helicopter made by Airbus Helicopters was a eight seater - the pilot plus six passengers i.e. two rows of four.

My wife sat in the front next to the pilot and me behind him next to the window. That said every seat had a great view. As wearing headphones is necessary in order to communicate we were all able to interact with the pilot who gave a great commentary. The whole flight including audio was recorded using a camera mounted on the front of the helicopter meaning that those of us who wanted to could purchase a copy along with a nice plaque including the pre-flight photograph.

Following take off we departed from the Grand Canyon South Rim over the Kaibab National Forest before reaching the rim of the Canyon that dropped away before us ....... this really was a spectacular view and incredible feeling. Flying over the Canyon we could see for miles. The North rim and eastern edge then cam into view something that many visitors don't see and nor would we if it hadn't been for the flight. We then followed the Colorado River and were able to see the water flowing at the foot of the Canyon. Flying through the widest and deepest part of the Canyon we were able to take as many photographs as we liked and in my case GoPro footage of almost the entire flight.

Crossing the Colorado River we left the Grand Canyon and returned to base.

On landing and once it was safe to alight we were able to take our own photographs around the helicopter including with our pilot.

We then returned to the terminal building where those of us who wanted could purchase a DVD recording of the flight and or plaque with our pre-flight photograph as a memento. We don't ordinarily purchase such things but this was a very special experience so we can now relive it with friends and family.

We have some amazing memories and great photographs. It was an incredible, beautiful and absolutely awesome experience that we would highly recommend.

If you want to do this don't wait until it's too late plan ahead to be sure you can get a flight.

Special thanks go to Daniel our pilot for making our experience so good.

Review Title: You will later regret if you do not do this
Review Text: I booked this helicopter ride directly Tripadvisor after having a few online chats with Maverick Helicopter. I think it may have been slightly cheaper through TripAdvisor (which went through a company called Viator). I got a confirmation of my 10:00am flight time, but later that evening (7 hrs later), I got an email from Viator saying that time was booked and I had to be moved to 11:30am. I was a little annoyed at this. I am not sure if Viator held my purchase for a while before passing it on to Maverick and the slot got filled in the meantime, or a larger group came in and they decided to bump me to accommodate the bigger group. I called Maverick directly saying this was a big inconvenience because I was only at the GC for two days and changing my time impacted  the other activities I had planned on my brief stay. Maverick was very understanding and said they would be able to work me in and I could keep my desired 10am slot. The flight was very, very smooth. Not one ounce of turbulence. If you had your eyes closed the whole time you would hardly be able to tell you left the ground. Our helicopter seated eight people including the pilot. Four seats up front, four in the back. They weigh each person when you check in and the computer balances out the copter. So, me and my oldest son were in the back middle, while my two younger/smaller sons had outside window views. I still had a perfect view from where I was sitting. When you take pictures from the middle you sometimes have to be careful how you aim the camera if you don't want part of the helicopter in the pic, but it's not a big issue. It did start raining while we were up, but after a minute or so it cleared up perfectly.Nice music plays gently in the background (mainly to add ambiance to the DVD should you purchase the in-flight recording), and with your headsets you can hear the pilot and talk to other people on the helicopter. The flight time was perfect and quite sufficient. I really felt I got my money's worth. The lobby of the facility is a very nice place to wait while you are awaiting your scheduled flight. I have no regrets and I know I have created an unforgettable family memory. I did the flight on 7-21-2017.

Review Title: Full potential of flight spoiled on Maverick Helicopter
Review Text: Some adventures are a once in a lifetime experience. This is true of our helicopter tour of the Grand Canyon. Unfortunately, we were randomly placed with a pilot whose playlist for background music was abrasive and, in light of the spiritual/sacred area, was offensive. Each pilot at Maverick chooses his/her own music. Ours chose heavy metal which blasted into our headphones. We could adjust the volume, but not the content even after mentioning the inappropriate nature of the sound track to the pilot. The only relief from the loud guitar twanging and drum beating came from Huey Lewis and the News. Really?  Huey Lewis while soaring above the Grand Canyon? Four of the six passengers were retired seniors. Why this music? The gift shops at the Canyon sell CDs of native music. I would like to suggest to Maverick , because music heightens or detracts from all experiences, that they use something more Zen-like as background. We saw the IMAX movie, Secrets of the Grand Canyon, excellent! The soundtrack provided appropriate emotional layering while viewing the vastness of the canyon in the IMAX setting. We highly recommend the helicopter tour of the canyon; it is something which defies description. Don't let the cost keep you from the experience. However, if you like a total experience, check your Maverick pilot's play list or work with a company (there are several) who understand the spirituality of our native people and do not insult it. No one at Maverick seemed interested in fielding our concern which was hugely disappointing. Please don't let this review keep you from the helicopter tour. Do it! But choose the company or pilot that will give you a total experience, not just incredible views of the canyon.

Review Title: Highly Recommended Once In A Lifetime Experience!
Review Text:
We pre-booked, online, an early morning “Canyon Spirit” flight from the Grand Canyon Airport.
We stayed overnight nearby in Tusayan and arrived at the airport at about 07:15 am for our “weigh in” and allocation to our helicopter and pilot.
Our pilot Ben gave us a flight safety briefing before allocating us to our seats and, as there were only five people on our flight, we were all lucky to have window seats!
We took off at about 07:50 am and flew over the Kaibab National Forest for about seven minutes before the ground dropped away and we flew off the edge above the Grand Canyon.
The views were stunning and the Grand Canyon was so vast it now felt that the helicopter was hovering! We flew over to the Eastern Side, along the North Rim then back to the Bright Angel/South Rim before returning to the airport about one hour later.
We had an excellent flight with a very interesting, knowledgeable and amusing commentary, from our pilot Ben, throughout our flight. We were very lucky to have excellent conditions with a bright blue sky, no wind, lots of sun and a very steady flight with no turbulence.
On arrival back we had time for a photo opportunity posing with Ben in front of our helicopter.
It was quite an expensive trip but it was worth it to be flown safely, on this once in a lifetime opportunity, by such a professional and efficient organisation.
Highly Recommended!

The plane flight was approximately 45 min in each direction. The plane was comfortable and offered a great perspective of the landscape below. It was a treat to move around the cabin mid-flight, Our teens enjoyed visiting the cockpit for a front row view.

The most thrilling portion of the trip was the 25 min helicopter flight over the canyon. This part is not to be missed! Our pilot Luke was amazing. There's not a bad seat in the house and the views are breathtaking.

The trolley ride was fun, our tour guide Bruce was polite, funny and offered interesting commentary. Your time on the ground is short but more than enough to appreciate the vastness and beauty of the canyon. Even the boxed lunch was better than expected.

If you are considering it, go for it. Worth every penny. It was the highlight of our trip!

Review Text:
We decided on the Maverick Helicopter Tour as it seemed that they had newer equipment than the other tour companies in the area. You meet at the Tusayan Airport which is outside of the Grand Canyon National Park (It is just outside of Tusayan). They have a large parking lot and guest services building with a gift shop, vending machines and restrooms. Check-in is fast and easy. They do take your weight (no lying about your weight, as you actually stand on a scale) which they use to assign your seating on the helicopter to balance the weight. You can request a front seat but they cannot guarantee specific seating but will give you preference if you ask in advance. Once everyone is checked in the pilot will call out your name and give you a seat assignment. You are provided with a life preserver that you wear around your waist and are assisted in getting in the helicopter. Once in, you put on your headphones and get a quick safety check. (you should wear dark clothing without prints so that you don't get a reflection off the inside of the glass when you take photos). The flight is about 45 minutes and there are no restrooms on the helicopter and no stops until you get back to the airport (as my Mother always told me, go now or forever hold your pees). The seats are very comfortable (seating for 7 including the pilot) and the helicopter is surprisingly quiet from others I have flown in. The weather was clear and the flight very calm and smooth.

Once everyone is secure the pilot takes off and introduces himself and finds out a little bit about you. You initially fly over the pine forests and listen to a play list and commentary through your headphones. Then you fly out over the Canyon itself. The view is spectacular as the trees and land immediately end and fall away from view and you are now hovering 4,000 feet above the Canyon Floor! The pilot forewarned us just before we cleared the trees and got our first panoramic view of the Canyon but it is still breathtaking! The pilot describes the various areas of the Canyon and sights and flies along both the South and North Rims as well as along the Colorado River. You can ask questions through your headsets and the pilot is more than happy to respond and elaborate on his narration. Although we viewed the Canyon from the South Rim, the Rim Trails, the Bright Angel Trail and the West Rim, this is a unique "not to miss" way to see the Canyon if your budget allows.

After about 45 minutes we landed back at the airport and they took pictures of us by the helicopter (with or without the pilot) and using their camera and ours. Although not required or requested, we did give a small gratuity to the pilot which I'm sure he appreciated. When we got back into the gift shop they had photos on the wall that you could purchase as well as a dvd of your specific flight made during the actual flight. Unfortunately the camera on our helicopter malfunctioned on our flight so we couldn't purchase the dvd of our flight but because we had asked to buy the dvd they gave us a complimentary copy of their generic dvd of the helicopter flight (very considerate and professional).

The price for the helicopter flight was about $300 per person for about 45 minutes but was well worth it. If you want to get a different perspective of the Grand Canyon, this is definitely not a tour to miss! I would highly recommend both the helicopter flight and Maverick Helicopters as the tour provider.

Review Title: A must-do for lovers of views and vistas!
Review Text: My husband and I, along with two other unrelated couples, had an excellent Grand Canyon Maverick Helicopters tour on Thanksgiving Day at noon, leaving from the Tusayan airport near the south rim. Our copter held 7 guests, so we had one extra space, which was nice. The seating arrangement is done by weight, so you may not get your optimum seat. (I would have picked next to the pilot looking ahead, but got a side window in the back row, which was fine. We didn't land again until the end, so no opportunity to change seats.) Our pilot, B.J., was calm, experienced, and personable. During the flight, he told us just the right amount of factoids about the canyon and the surrounding park while an apropos soft rock soundtrack, curated by B.J., played through our headphones, changing for each phase of the flight. The gray leather seats were comfortable (although not rotating) and there were excellent views available, both near and far as we flew in different directions over the sunny south rim and the snowy north rim and (mostly) in between them, looking down at the cliffs and Colorado River far below us. The 30+-minute canyon tour was a good length for appreciating the scope and grandeur of the canyon, although I could have spent all day out there gliding over those views! The take-off and landing couldn't have been smoother, and the spacious Maverick waiting room (with fireplace & restrooms) and gift-store are top notch. They took photos of us at the beginning and end standing by the copter, and then as we were leaving offered us an official photo and DVD to commemorate our flight. A memorable Thanksgiving Day, that's for sure! (One photo tip: Wear black if you don't want to see yourself reflected in the windows as you shoot your photos.)

Review Text:
Wir hatten einen fantastischen, angenehmen und kurzweiligen Flug mit dem sehr gut gelaunten und unterhaltsamen Piloten BJ inklusive passender Musik-Einspielung ins Intercom (also im Kopfhörer)

Die Längere Tour ist nur ein klein wenig teurer, aber dafür viel länger als die kürzere Tour.

Wir hatten uns schon vorher die verschiedenen Anbieter etwas angesehen und uns dann für Maverick entscheiden, was sich vor Ort auch als die richtige Wahl herausstellte. Ohne behaupten zu wollen, dass die anderen es schlecht machen, gibt sich Maverick m.E. noch ein klein wenig mehr Mühe und achtet noch ein klein wenig mehr auf einen sicheren Ablauf und Flug. So tankt Maverick z.B. (anders als andere) die Helis nicht bei laufendem Motor auf und die Passagiere steigen nur ein und aus, wenn die Rotorblätter komplett still stehen. Kleinigkeiten, die nicht viel ausmachen mögen und die einem wahrscheinlich kaum auffallen, wenn man sich nicht generell bissi mit Luftfahrt beschäftigt, m.E. aber ein wenig für die Abläufe und Gedanken im Hintergrund sprechen. Bei schlechtem Wetter und zu tief hängenden Wolken wird nicht geflogen (darf auch nicht, da Sichtflug und man ist immerhin auf über 1600m Höhe), bei zu viel Wind bleiben die Helis am Boden und dann wird auch nichts berechnet. Generell buchen die erst direkt vor dem Flug ab.

Maverick achtet schon darauf, dass der Kunde etwas für sein Geld bekommt und nicht mit gefüllter K…tüte aus dem Fluggerät aussteigt. Storno (bis 48h vorher) oder kurzfristige Verlegung sind kein Problem – wir hatten wegen durchziehendem Tiefdruck-Trog und vorhersehbar viel Wind zunächst storniert, sind dann aber einen Tag später doch geflogen und haben es ganz sicher nicht bereut.

Die Sitze in den geflogenen EC-130 Helis haben alle Sicht nach vorne, so dass man auch von den Mittelsitzen auf der Rückbank noch gut sehen kann. Fensterplätze sind natürlich besser. Die Sitzzuweisung erfolgt nach Computerberechnung gemäß optimaler Balance des Fluggerätes, d.h. man sitzt ggf. auch nicht nebeneinander, selbst wenn man zu zweit bucht

 

Ein einmaliges Erlebnis und auch den sicher nicht ganz geringen Preis wert. Für Maverick 100% Empfehlung

Review Text:

However, this could be the best $299 per person that you ever spend. I have always wanted to see the Grand Canyon. In fact, it is the only piece of travel on my "bucket list". Believe me, the Grand Canyon from a helicopter will not disappoint! This is one of those once-in-a-lifetime experiences that you will never, ever forget. Our pilot (Marshall) was excellent and pointed out all sort of features along the Canyon.

What I did like was that they took photos of everyone before they got on the helicopter and did the usual superimposed pictures for you to buy at the end of the trip. However, they also allowed everyone to take their own pictures using their own cameras and even took the pictures for you. Review Text:
We took the Canyon Spirit tour, which leaves in the late afternoon and catches the sun's rays slanting into the Canyon. Helicopter tours are not cheap for most of us, but there is no doubt that it is a trip to remember. We flew in great weather, found the office check-in smooth and professional, and our pilot Danny was friendly and engaging and pointed out many a spectacular sight during our trip.

I was sandwiched in the back without a direct window seat (they seat you appropriately to balance the aircraft), so I could not snap the kinds of pics I would have liked (though my partner had a window seat and was able to do so). Nevertheless, the trip reminded me of the original timbre of that over-used Americanism "awesome".

Make sure your cellphones/cameras are completely charged up. Mine ran out of juice toward the end of the 45-minute tour, as did another passenger's.

The entire flight is video-recorded (camera faces straight out the aircraft nose), and you can purchase a copy (complete with music and passenger "oohs" and ahhs") after the trip for about $40. Here is my only criticism of the tour. Not only do I think that $40 is gouging the customer, but I found the quality of the video to be quite low. Add to this that the lens had some kind of smear on it from beginning to end, and it shows up quite obviously in the final product. The current camera set up also does not compensate well for situations in which the canyon walls are in relative shadow compared to the sun's rays slanting over the canyon rim; this results in not being able to see much of anything in the final product for extended stretches. If you are taking the evening or morning tours, keep this in mind.

Overall, though, a fantastic experience and one I would happily repeat some day.

Review Text: Highly recommend seeing the Grand Canyon from the air.  There are a couple of helicopter tours that leave out of the Tusayan airport.  Maverick is on the back side, or the second entrance coming from the town.  We took a 45 minute tour which was a good amount of time for us.  During check in you, and anything you will be carrying on the helicopter, are weighed.  The scale reading is displayed on the computer screen, behind the counter.  The company uses this information to distribute the weight on the helicopter.  The helicopter seating arrangement is the pilot plus three people in the front; and four people across the back.  We only had the pilot plus 5 passengers, so the two center backseat chairs were empty.  Maverick says all seats have a view, but not really.  Those two seats don't have an unobstructed view in any direction. However, if you're feeling anxious about it, maybe those are the seats for you.  But, in my opinion, looking down is the reason seeing the Grand Canyon from the air is so amazing. You wear a 4 point harness.  The helicopter rotors were stopped before we got on and off.  Our pilot was okay.  My impression is that he was newer to the area and didn't have much additional information outside the script. But I guess we all start somewhere.  He was professional and our flight was smooth.  The only stomach dip was when we flew over the rim going into the canyon for the first time.  The tour we took didn't go very deeply into the canyon.  It was an incredible view.  After the flight we were able to take lots of pictures, and weren't rushed at all.  They also sell a video of your flight.

Review Text: Perfect day! We were collected from our hotel at 5.10am, the driver arrived exactly on time. It was an early start but worth it as we were first at the skywalk and guano point which meant we could walk straight on. Flight to canyon was very smooth. Our pilot Lindsay was lovely, explained everything and really put us all at ease. It was a bit hazy so Lindsay skipped flying over the Hoover dam and lake mead and took us there on the flight back instead so we had a better view. The plane seated 8 and our family of 4 shared with another family of 4. Once landed we boarded buses to the sky walk and guano point. We had a choice of eating our meal at either location. We chose guano point which is a barbecue type meal. It was a bit weird to be eating mash potatoes and chicken at 9am but we were hungry being up so early and the food was delicious. Next we boarded the helicopter and landed down in the canyon. It was hot but an amazing experience. Another great pilot called Jerry. We were then met by Lindsay again and flown back to Vegas. All in all a fantastic day, expensive but so worth it. Maverick Helicopters are a professional company who treat you like VIPs. You can tell safety is a priority. Everything ran like clockwork. We heard other people complain about the other tour operators on the day saying they were late which meant they did not have enough time. We had plenty of time at each location. Would defiantly reccomend this tour and Maverick.

Review Text:

The pilot will tell you where to sit based on weight.

I have also taken a Maverick tour leaving from Las Vegas over the West rim, and I found both experiences amazing for different reasons. The trip over the South rim and the National Park was spectacular and the views, colours and depth of the Grand canyon where breathtaking. A highlight was the Colorado river and its amazing turquoise colour. While the trip leaving Las Vegas was also amazing, going over Hoover dam, travelling over the strip then landing in the Hualapai Reservation for a champagne lunch. The actual depth of West rim is not as deep as the views over the National park South rim.

Many people will go on about how the trips leaving from Las Vegas is not actually over Grand Canyon National park, while this is completely true the experience in my opinion is no less of a thrill and no less breathtaking. I have to say I like them both for different reasons. I would have no hesitation in recommending either trip as both are amazing and you certainly do not miss out on breathtaking views doing either of them.

Review Text:
Yes, $280 is a lot of money. Aviation is expensive, it's just one of those unchangeable things. Bear in mind though, a ten minute helicopter flight in the UK will cost you around £70 ($100). $280 for forty five minutes - at the Grand Canyon, no less! - is an absolute bargain.

The helicopters are ECO-Star EC-130s and are flown by ex-military pilots, if the chap who flew us was to be believed. The helis will seat eight people in two rows and the seating arrangement is determined by the pilot according to weight. I was assigned to the front, second from the right. The view was excellent, albeit slightly disconcerting as it's pretty much just glass in every direction, including underfoot. Another member of my party was seated in a central seat in the back row and I imagine that her view was not particularly good. Unfortunately, it's just pot luck as to which seat you get.

Our pilot wasn't the most friendly person, but he got us around safely and that's really what matters. One small niggle that I had was that I'm a light aircraft pilot myself and I wasn't entirely comfortable with how close we were flying to the peaks and pinnacles sometimes, nor with how much traffic was in certain areas. However, this may have just been a "control freak" issue because I couldn't hear the radio and was acutely aware of the presence of the other aircraft. I'm the same when I'm a passenger in someone else's car, so... yeah.

A few final pointers: make sure you budget for it, make sure you book in advance, make sure you take photo ID with you, bear in mind that flights may be cancelled if the weather is unfit for flying or if there are too few passengers for the flight to be viable - always call a few hours before your flight to check.

Good points: HELICOPTER! AT THE GRAND CANYON!

Bad points: a bit impersonal.

Our pilot - young, handsome and very knowledgeable (Rivers), was very pleasant during the entire tour, from explaining details pre-flight to being in the air, he knew everything one needed to know about the Grand Canyon, even the sights that formed a dragon to the names of each temple shaped grounds. The flight was very interesting and we felt immediately that safety was on their top priority as Rivers explained about the winds and the turbulence we would be experiencing during flight.

We all filled the special bags during the flight, and amazingly on arrival we were greeted with cool towels and bottles of water as Rivers radioed in the request before arrival. His attention was amazing and a true asset to the company.

We would have loved to have our trip on the DVD but unfortunately they had technical problems but they provided us with a generic DVD of a heli tour on the Grand Canyon. Not as special, as it was a lifetime experience and our very first heli ride, but better than nothing.

If you are planning to see the beauty of the Grand Canyon from the air, the best way to go is with Meverick Helicopters, they know their stuff and their hospitality is excellent. Well worth the monies spent!

Review Title: Used money from my retirement for this...AND IT WAS WORTH IT!!!
Review Text:
So, it's been on my bucket list for years to visit the Grand Canyon. My cousin went and told me she took a helicopter ride into the Canyon. I looked at her like she was crazy and she simply explained, "I don't know when I'll ever go back, so I did it big." When I found out my husband was going to Vegas for business and we would have a free day, I decided that it was worth it to use some of our retirement money that had recently been cashed in and to make it big. I may never go back. I may die before retirement age. It was a once in a lifetime trip for me to cross off the item at the top of my bucket list. IT WAS WORTH IT!!

So here is what we did. A van picked us up at our hotel. We stopped to pick up another couple at another hotel. They drove us to the airport. We took a small plane with 3 other couples and flew over the Hoover Dam. We took tons of photos. We landed and went over immediately to our Helicopter. We took off and we all had on ear phones and could hear each other. The pilot meant to play music but forgot to, I'm glad he did. He flew towards the Canyon and then took a dip into it and you could hear the other passengers gasping and saying Wow. It literally took your breathe away. The front of the helicopter was all glass so it was like we were floating in the Canyon. I literally had tears in my eyes.

We landed in the Canyon and got out and were able to spend a decent amount of time in the Canyon walking around and taking pictures, for about 20 minutes. Then we boarded the helicopter in different seats and flew back to where we took off. Then we boarded a bus and went to two different look out areas on the Canyon. One has the glass floor you walk out on. The view was amazing. The second look out area included a huge delicious meal served to us by the friendly local native Americans.

On the way back to get back to our plane to go back, I realized I lost my iphone. The employees at Maverick went out of their way, along with one of the park staff members to help me find and retrieve my phone. We boarded the plane and flew back over the Hoover Dam and people on the other side of the plane got great pictures this time. We landed at the airport and the shuttle van took us back to our hotel.

The pilot was AMAZING. The whole trip was worth EVERY SINGLE PENNY. I CAN NOT RECOMMEND THIS ENOUGH. My husband made video of the helicopter flight and showed it to all his co-workers and that was all it took for them to want to do this.

Shortly after take off we couldn't see anything from the windows for the 50 min flight to the South Rim Grand Canyon because of rain clouds / fog. There were 14 of us and we transferred to a Maverick bus and went to x2 viewpoints on the canyon rim but there was nothing to see it was completely enveloped in thick swirling fog. When we returned to the bus the guide informed us that the helicopter flights had been cancelled. So we boarded the plane and transferred back to Henderson.
It was here that we were informed that we would be partially refunded the portion of the Helicopter flight. I am afraid that I don't have the words to describe the feeling of seeing such a staggering sight spreading out for miles and miles all around us. This tour isn't cheap at $299 per person, however the memories are priceless. Review Text:
We took the Canyon Spirit flight at 9am September 18. We had great weather and a great flight. Winds were calm and there was no turbulence. I booked the flight for four people a couple of weeks before our trip. The Maverick helicopters on this route seat seven passengers (3 in the front, four in the back seat). I figured that this gave of a five out of seven chance of getting a good seat for my wife who is 5' 1". I did not want her to be stuck in a middle set in the back due to her height. We checked in the morning of the flight and had to be weighed. A person's weight is only visible to the person working behind the counter, so one need not feel embarrassed. As luck turned out only one other person was scheduled for our flight so everyone got either a front or window seat. Ben, our pilot, was knowledgeable about the area and spoke to us over the headsets throughout the flight, pointing out features and discussing history of the park. He had a great sense of humor which made the flight more enjoyable. He also paid attention to each passenger so that no one felt left out. The views of the canyon were breathtaking especially when we first flew over the edge and the canyon floor fell away. While the flight was not cheap, it was well worth the money. It was the highlight of our 2 week vacation to Arches and Grand Canyon National Parks. After the flight while purchasing photos and a DVD of OUR flight, my sister asked if they had a military discount since she and he husband were serving. We were told no for the merchandise but were told the flight did. After verifying the military ID, the staff went out of their way to manually reverse the charges for the already paid for flight and then charged the rate with a ten percent discount.
Kudos to Maverick.

Review Title: Not a Bump in the Sky!
Review Text:
We did pre-book (via Titan tours UK) and flew at 9 am, weighed and put into groups so you will fly with other people, 6 in our helicopter. You get pre-flight notes to read and a small life preserver to wear (scary) in case you ditch into the Colorado river!

The take off was so smooth, straight up and you skim above the trees. They pipe music into your headphones like from 'Top Gun' and your pilot also talks you through everything, landmarks, speed etc. It takes a good 5 minutes to get to the rim of the grand canyon and I was very nervous about this part as I had heard that the 'up draft' will make it bumpy or push you upwards but no absolutely no change in our flight.

You think you are hovering but get told your speed is 200 kph. The view from up top is unbelievable, you just do not grasp the size of this place otherwise.

I would say to anyone put a helicopter flight on your list of 'Must do's' for the Grand Canyon.

I would also mention that when we later visited the rim in the afternoon by bus it was quite windy, is morning the best time for a flight?

Review Title: Awesome - a MUST when you visit Grand Canyon.
Review Text:
The Maverick Helicopter Tours is a very smoothly and professionally run business. Great staff in the reception building. You have restrooms here, a gift shop and a cafeteria.
The helicopters look brand new. They are specifically designed for sightseeing tours and offer excellent views for the three passengers in the front row and the two passengers in the back row seated by the windows. The two passengers in the middle seats of the back row have somewhat less good views.
I went on the 45 minute Weather Route, which gives you the longest time over the Canyon. Our pilot Justin was very nice, knowledgable and a really professional pilot.
This is really the best way to truly appreciate the grandness and beauty of the Grand Canyon. I highly recommend this tour. It is a bit pricey, but that goes for all helicopter sightseeing tours around the world.

The one thing I regret was being one of the interior passengers in the second row of the helicopter. The two interior seats of the back row have the worst views. The pilot assigns the seating, theoretically by weight distribution, but our flight was all about the same and I got the middle by luck of the draw. The whole trip was brilliant from start to finish and was even enjoyed by my wife who hates flying.

Everyone constantly made sure that we were ok and provided a stream of information about the Grand Canyon.

The only - very minor - hiccup was that our trip had to be moved from the morning to the afternoon but Maverick contacted me as soon as possible by phone and email to make sure that I received the message and offered a choice of alternative dates and times.

Overall a fantastic trip and a helicopter tour of the Grand Canyon is highly recommended!!

Review Title: Loved landing inside the canyon! Like a slo-mo of Thelma and Louise going off the cliff but without the sad ending.
Review Text:
Loved this tour. This was my first time in a helicopter and it was amazing! all the staff from the shuttle driver to the pilot were really knowledgeable and friendly. The hanger where you wait is great - lots of souvenirs, photos of the area and a little cafe. It's a nice, big open space to wait for your flight.

The flight out to the Grand Canyon was I'd guess just over twenty minutes and you pass over Lake Mead and the Hoover Dam. The pilot will give you lots of information about the area sprinkled with some little know facts and some humour. flying into the Grand Canyon and landing was amazing. The only downside is they don't give you enough time inside the canyon. We were landed and back out within half an hour - I could've spent a couple hours walking around the area. But they have a great landing spot with an amazing view for photos. The snack is not much more than what you would get on a standard airplane ride but you could bring your own snack and they give you some champagne!

On the flight back they stop for fuel (or at least they did on our trip) so you get another experience with landing and taking off. The stop is all of five minutes so not much waiting around but if I were the company I'd set up something at the landing spot just to give the tourists something to do...even if it's just some cheesy photo boards with those face holes cut in them for personal photos...or plant some different species of desert cactus or something. Although they probably want to discourage guests from venturing too far from their helicopter while it's refueling.

Overall this was an extravagant tour for us but it was totally worth it and we had such a good time. But...we got engaged on the tour so we might be a little biased to how awesome it was.

Review Title: A genuine highlight, but not stress free! - July 11th 2015
Review Text:
Sorry - this is a long review, but there is some constructive feedback at the end which needs reading.

Having booked with Maverick airlines last year to fly from Vegas to the South Rim on a small plane tour, one regret was not taking up the option of a helicopter flight. This year my wife, daughter and I had planned another road trip but coming at the Canyon from a different direction - on the train from Williams.

My first interaction with Maverick was by live chat on their website in February '15. Spoke to a lady called Elaine who was helpful and informative. My big question: the train arrives at 11:45am and leaves at 3.15pm - what would be the best option for a 40 minute Canyon Spirit tour? She suggested the 12:45 flight, with 12:15 check in. It would be 20 minutes in a cab from the train depot so plenty of time. No they don't have their own transport but cabs would be readily available and she gave me the number to call one in advance.

I wanted more time to think it through before booking and it was May before I felt confident to reserve 3 seats on Saturday the 11th July at 12:45. Maverick advised me that we were the only 3 on the flight and that they'd need at least 3 more before they'd fly. Same instruction as last year - call the day before to check in and confirm the flight.

Our holiday itinerary meant we'd be on the road a lot during office hours. I called Maverick from San Diego 2 days before to confirm and they told me they had still not sold any other seats but not to worry, they usually do. 12 hours later we were in Williams with the train the next morning. Called again - yes they had enough seats sold so the flight would go ahead.

At this point I started worrying about the taxi. I called the phone number to book one. Unobtainable. I googled cabs in the Grand Canyon, but only Flagstaff numbers came up. Just have to wing it then.

Arrived at Grand Canyon depot at 11:45 - no cabs. Asked a park ranger who gave me a number for Xanterra who arrange cabs, but no service on the mobile. 20 minutes passed and we were panicking. We ran into the El Tovar and asked the concierge for help - she called Xanterra who said it would be 45 minutes…+ 20 to the airport = flight missed. She called Maverick for us and I spoke to a guy…he left me on hold a while and came back to tell me a car would be there in 9 minutes.

We arrived at the airport at 12:35, sweating! From that point we relaxed. We got weighed and bags stored. Our pilot for the day was BJ, who took us out to the helicopter for quick introductions.

There were 6 people on the flight, organised by weight. The helicopter has 2 banks of seats, with 3 available in front and 4 in rear. My wife and daughter were in the front row and I was rear left. Views were exceptional in the front seats and excellent for me in the back. Not so sure how people in the middle of rear would have found it. But it's luck of the draw. If you are light and slim, you will likely be in the front.

BJ was an entertaining and informative host and kept us all interested and engaged throughout the flight. The first 5 minutes of the flight took us over trees and scrub, towards the lip of the canyon. Then jaws literally dropped as BJ took us over the edge. Imagine sitting on a rollercoaster as it attempts its vertical drop…now imagine that drop is 6,000 feet down! What a feeling! There was significant clutching going on as fingernails gripped seats.

For the rest of the flight we navigated from south to north and back. The colours, the lines of evolution, the difference in vegetation - its not something you can easily see just walking around the rim, but up in the air the stunning vista opens up magically.

On return we found that Maverick had organised for us to share a cab back to the South Rim so we could get our return train. In summary, Maverick provided us with a genuine highlight of our holiday, rescued us from potential disaster and stopped up when they needed to. for that, it was a 5* experience.

However, I have some constructive criticism to make re the booking process:

Shuttle transport should be available to get clients from the South Rim to the airport. If you book as a package with the train company, or with Maverick airlines as part of a tour you do. As an independent booking you don't. It would take away the stress completely to know that you would be picked up and dropped off at the right time. Both trips cost us $22 + tip. I'd be happy to see this included in the overall price, just for peace of mind.

The on-line live chat team should be aware of the cab limitations from the train depot at GCSR. We were told that cabs would be readily available but on Saturday at peak time, only 3 cabs were running at one time. For the volume of visitors this seems destined for disaster. As the entire cab (and it's really a mini-bus) operation is operated by Xanterra there are no alternative options.

We highly recommend the Canyon Spirit Tour on Maverick helicopters. It gave us a fresh experience of the canyon. However, I would make sure you book either a package or have transport arranged for you before you arrive at the park.

Review Text:
"Best hour of my life"--or at least that's how my daughter (not a little kid, but rather a highly accomplished and well travelled professional) described it. While I trust her exclamation was hyperbolic, I certainly understand her sentiments, even if I don't share her newly acquired ambition to purchase a helicopter. The Grand Canyon is vast, some 277 miles long. Short of a couple of weeks on a raft on the Colorado river, or a very very long hike, it is impossible to appreciate fully the majesty and expanse of this natural wonder other than by air. I'm a confirmed believer in enjoying landscapes slowly and under my own power and don't usually go in for this sort of thing, but the Maverick tour leaving from Tusayan left me breathless and was worth every penny (and it takes a lot of pennies to fly with Maverick). Maverick uses aircraft explicitly designed for sightseeing, which means extra glass, stadium seating, all seats facing forward and somewhat less noise and vibration (although you will certainly still need to wear the supplied noise cancelling headphones). Other companies do not necessarily use these specially purposed copters. Since all companies follow the same route, your choice basically depends on the kind of aircraft they fly and the quality of the pilot. Our pilot was tremendously knowledgeable, mixed a good deal of information with a bit of humor and made every effort to insure a pleasant and relaxed experience for all. We happened to have the great good fortune to sit in the front row of seats which undoubtedly offer a superior experience--you can request the front row, but ultimately seating is determined by the need to distribute passenger weight. We took the longer 45 minute tour (which actually lasted closer to an hour); there isn't much difference in price compared to shorter flights from Tusayan, and I can see no reason why anyone would opt for less time over the canyon, short of a fear of heights in which case they don't belong on this trip anyway. I won't attempt to describe the sights you will see, since words can not do justice to the undulating otherworldly beauty of this place. Its as simple as this: If you are going to the trouble of visiting the Grand Canyon and can afford the fare, take this flight! Economize if need be on accommodations or meals (you can eat anywhere) and take this flight! (I've spent 8 years regretting not taking a helicopter over the Na-apali coast on Kauai--avoid my folly!)
Oh, there is one negative: The staff at the terminal are unhelpful, borderline rude, our flight departed 30 minutes early, we were hustled aboard and were not informed until the last minute that you can't bring pretty much anything aboard other than a camera and a bottle of water, forcing us to make some rather hurried adjustments. (Do bring your camera rather than paying the outrageous fees they will charge you for a video of your flight or a family photo). Bottom line: Maverick ain't great on the ground, but once airborne, its a nearly transcendental experience.
