Review Title: Canyon Spirit Helicopter Tour: add this to your bucket list!
Review Text:
Halfway through our 45-minute tour, our pilot, BJ, asked us to let him know as soon as he'd made it to the top of our "coolest thing ever done" list. I replied, "You hit that the second we headed over the edge of the canyon!" Truly, that moment 7 minutes into the flight when we shot off the plateau of Kaibab National Forest and the Grand Canyon opened up beneath us is something I'll never forget, not to mention the unbelievable views throughout the rest of the tour.

Maverick Helicopters offers several tours in Nevada and Arizona, and reviews of different ones are combined here on TA; make sure to focus on the reviews for the specific tour you're considering taking. My review applies only to the Canyon Spirit Helicopter Tour, which departs from the South Rim Helicopter Terminal, about 6 miles south of the Grand Canyon National Park entrance, perfect for people driving themselves.

BJ was the ideal pilot: wicked sense of humour, very proactive about sharing interesting facts about the geology of the canyon, and able to answer every question thrown at him. I noted that he was also simply amazing at taking away the nervousness of the two little girls who, along with their dad, had the front seats, and he kept them engaged with jokes and questions throughout the flight.

My father and I were fortunate to each get window seats in the back row. A window seat is a must if you plan to take decent photos (a major goal for me) as you need to put your camera right against the glass to avoid reflections. Anyone stuck in a middle rear seat would not only miss photo ops but also have quite a restricted view. Currently, Maverick offers no way to reserve a specific seat position in advance, so you pays your money and you takes your chance. Since many of the negative reviews on TA reflect unhappiness with seat assignments, I'll bet that Maverick would find plenty of takers for special flights with reduced passenger numbers that avoid the need to stick anyone in a rear middle seat—I'd certainly have paid a lot more for that guarantee. This would still allow the pilot to assign the prime seating as needed to balance weight.

Be aware too that the pilots play music throughout the flight, and since musical tastes differ, you may not be keen on their choice. I wasn't (hard rock's not my scene), but honestly the Grand Canyon was so mind-blowing that BJ could have played an album of Inuit throat singing and I probably wouldn't have minded. I'll bet you find the same.

As mementos, you can purchase a photo of yourself with the pilot taken by a Maverick staff member at the start of the flight, and a DVD of your specific tour taken by the video camera mounted underneath the chopper, which includes the audio of all cockpit conversations and the background music. You are free to take photos to your heart's content during the flight (don't forget to pack extra memory cards), but not on the ground on the helipad, for legitimate safety reasons.

Check-in was quick and friendly. They need to weigh you for weight distribution on the chopper, but this is painless as the scale is built into the floor at the check-in desk; don't worry if you're not proud of your stats, as they don't broadcast your number to the room or even mention it to you. Note that you're not allowed to bring a backpack or handbag on board, so plan accordingly. I had my camera on a shoulder strap, and that was no problem.

My 80-year-old dad was grinning ear-to-ear throughout the flight, and hasn't stopped raving about it since. This tour is absolutely worth the $274 per person charge; I give it my highest recommendation. Heartfelt thanks to BJ and the Maverick ground crew for a priceless memory.

We booked the tour by phone. Arriving at Grand Canyon airport, we found Maverick to be well organized and professional. We were weighed and paid. Then we waited a few minutes before meeting our pilot, Brett.

We got a quick safety lesson and were fitted with flotation devices. Then we were seated according to weight. Brett is very experienced so we were following a less experienced pilot for training. Soon, we were airborne.

Helicopter rides are always special. But there's nothing like flying over a ponderosa pine/juniper forest a few hundred feet over the land and abruptly being 5000 feet ( 1 mile) above the awesome Grand Canyon!

The mighty Colorado river was beautiful. Brett pointed out lots of geological formations and types of strata in the canyon walls. He also pointed out some sacred native locations. The whole experience was fabulous!

The tour lasted about 1 1/2 hours. You can buy dvds of your flight for 39.95 and photos of you for 19.95.

Tip about tips: pilot school is expensive and the pilots appreciate gratuities.

Review Text:
First helicopter ride for us and we liked it.

We departed from the Grand Canyon airport, and be aware that Maverick is the second airport turn after the turnaround, not the first.

The reception area is very modern and nice. You have to pay, show ID, get weighed (done very discreetly), and read an advisory page before meeting the pilot (who will call your name when he is ready to roll).

There were 3 other people sharing our flight. The pilot does introductions, provides a short trip and safety briefing, and then takes you out to the machine. They snap pictures of you with the helicopter and pilot (to sell upon return), do a few more safety briefing things, have you snap on an inflatable flotation device around your waist, and then place you inside the machine. They use your weight to determine where you should sit and you may not sit next to your party. We soon understood that isn't a big deal as you also must wear headphones and speak into a microphone so everyone hears everything said for the entire trip so it's not like you can be whispering to your spouse anyway. You also get belted in via a 3 point system that is pretty robust. You have to sort of climb in, and there is a guy to help. It is no harder than getting into a mini-van. The cabin is heated/cooled so you don't need a coat. It seemed like the back row seats were a bit more spacious--but they all may be the same. One of us sat in front, and one in back, and we thought the views were equally good.

The pilot is very good at describing both the aspects of the ride, and also the Canyon below. The best "buzz" feeling is when the helicopter first goes over the canyon after the run over the woods--it is pretty thrilling.

The entire ride was smooth as glass and we never had a whiff of fear. It was really both thrilling and calming.

This is a fairly expensive attraction, but we thought it was worth the money. Upon landing there is opportunity to ask more questions and take more pictures, and they also offer to sell you their professional-taken picture just before take-off, and also a CD. The pilot lingers to see if anyone is going to tip him and that is a bit awkward but there is zero pressure.

We were glad we went.

Review Text:
Expensive? I guess it depends on your income and perspective. I've paid more (much more) than this for a single night in a hotel. This was my first ride in a helicopter, which made it especially interesting. The weather was perfect the day we went out. Pretty smooth ride; no one got sick. Our uniformed pilot was very professional and attentive to everyone's needs. They equip you with headphones and microphones that allow you to communicate with others. They also play some theme music over the headphones that helps to set the mood. We started out flying low over some flat wooded areas, and they played that Wagner composition from Apocalypse Now. It was kind of like heading out for an attack mission in 'Nam! Then suddenly the bottom drops and you are over the Grand Canyon. Then they play music from Star Wars and 2001. You don't just hover high above, they also take you in close to many rock formations so they are right next to you or right below you. The length was just right. I certainly did not feel like it was over too soon. I went the day after Thanksgiving when it was really busy at the park, but still didn't see many other aircraft in the area. Then we returned with some Indiana Jones music.

Life-altering? I wouldn't go that far. But for me, it definitely fit into the category of "show me something I haven't seen before". One more thing to cross off my bucket list.

Review Text: Was the helicopter ride expensive? More than two nights' hotel accommodation (Best Western, Tusayan) and meals! But for an unparalleled perspective of the canyon, including the surprise of your life when your get to the canyon, you can't buy the experience anywhere else. The round trip from lift off to touch down was about 55 min, and the route (because of FAA rules) traverses parts of the canyon one normally sees. Go late in the day, when the later afternoon sun helps reveal the rocks' colors and shadows accentuate the topography. Expect a wait, even if you have reservations: flights are filled in order booked, but these have to be mitigated by passenger weights so the load is safe and balanced. In our case, we arrived after some others but because our weights (we're lighter than the average North American) were within the range they needed to fill up a load (typically 6 passengers), we kind of jumped the queue (to the vocal displeasure of one couple). Other than that, you'll get a supremely capable pilot who has a broad knowledge of local nature and geology. Don't look upon the cost as a luxury - look upon it as adding a third dimension to your otherwise level perspective.

Review Text: We arrived in good time and after  paying and being weighed for the correct distribution within the helicopter, we sat and waited for the 3 other passengers. The area you sit and wait has a variety of tshirts, baseball caps and other souvenirs, the seating is comfortable and the whole area clean and spacious. The staff were all very friendly and accommodating. I explained that as I can suffer with claustrophobia, if possible could they place me near the side not in the middle. The other three passengers only just made it in time. As we were on the 4pm flight and they have to clear the canyon by 5pm, the staff told us if they hadn't been on time, they would have taken off without them. We were relieved as it is expensive and we wouldn't have wanted to have our experience, which we had looked forward to for so long, cut short. Our pilot was Brad, a lovely person who we felt completely comfortable and confident with. We were given the safety briefing and got on board. I was thrilled to find that I was seated at the front next to the door, fabulous views. Not sure if this was after my request or just luck :-) We took off and flew over the pine forest. As I have never been in a helicopter before I wasn't sure what to expect. It was a lot smoother than I thought it would be, I felt comfortable and safe. We approached the canyon with Brad saying that if we had a camera, turn it on now. I took a video with my phone. As we approached and then flew out over the canyon everyone just said ....WWWOOOOAHHHHH. It was like the bottom just dropped out of your world, incredible. no amount of words can describe it really, no amount of looking at photos, you just have to see it for yourself. Brad was excellent, giving commentary on points of interest and answering our questions, which he encouraged us to do. As I just couldn't get perspective on the immensity of it all, I pointed out a particular elevation and asked Brad how tall it was. He answered, 3 Empire State buildings. That gave us all perspective and helped us understand the size of the canyon, just amazing. The whole flight was just fantastic. My only minus point was that as we had opted for the 4pm flight, the sun was low (we wanted a later flight to get the shades and colours) and at times washed out the colours on the way back, but by no means diluted the experience. Brad flew a couple of times into shade to give us the best possible experience. We landed and photos were taken with the copter. All in all an unforgettable experience and what a way to spend my 50th birthday. I would heartily recommend this company to anyone wanting this flight over the Canyon. Just wonderful!

Review Text:
We booked this flight as an upgrade with another company that was taking us to the South Rim by mini van.
We were dropped off at Grand Canyon airport about 12.00 for our flight at half past.
First they weigh you, so they know how to distribute the weight in the helicopter.
Obviously this means you don't have a choice of where you sit on the helicopter. 2 of us were in the front, & 2 of us in the back by the window, & the next seat in.
The front seats are best, but you can still see well from the back.
Our pilot Marcus was great, & gives you the usual safety advice, shows you how to buckle the seat belt, & helps with your life jacket.
He encourages you to speak over the headset that you wear, & ask questions, as this comes out on the DVD that you can buy afterwards.
You fly low over the tree's for a while, & then you reach the edge of the Canyon, & it was amazing. As none of us had seen it from the edge yet, it was probably better for us.
The pilot explained everything on the flight, pointing out the names of rock formations, & a herd of Buffalo over on the North Rim. Also the Little Colorado river, & some rafters on the Colorado river.
All in all, it was about a 50 minute flight, & it made the long drive out there worth it.
The DVD is great, & we believe worth the money.
We will do it again one day, & would highly recommend it.

Review Text:
The flight over the Grand Canyon is one of the most amazing things I have ever done and it something that I will remember for a very long time. It is ABSOLUTLEY BRILLIANT and I would highly recommend it to anyone. If there were a list of things that you simply must do before you die, this would have to be somewhere in the top ten. Seeing the Grand Canyon from the air enables you to appreciate it in a way which is just not possible from the ground. The pilot was extremely friendly and enthusiastic, ensuring that all the passengers were eager and excited before we have even taken off, and his commentary and overall professionalism during the flight made the experience all the more enjoyable.

I took my flight from Maverick Helicopter’s base at Grand Canyon Airport, near Tusayan. They offer a pleasant waiting area and sell refreshments, t-shirts and souvenirs. The flight itself is recorded, and you have the option afterwards of buying a souvenir DVD of your own actual flight, together with a photograph of yourself standing next to the helicopter before take-off.

If you have previously taken a helicopter ride over a city, it is possible that you may have thought that it was good but not great, or that it was a lot of money to pay for quite a short experience and perhaps not worth the cost. If this is the case, do not let that put you off. Having also taken helicopter rides over cities, I can say that the Grand Canyon experience is in a completely different league, and whilst on a city flight you may get only around 15 or 20 minutes, here you get a good 40 minutes or more in the air.

The flight currently costs $275 per person (plus tip, plus cost of souvenir photo, DVD, T-shirt etc.!) A common response I had in the days immediately afterwards when raving about the trip to other people and trying to persuade them to do it was “But it is very expensive”. It is of course perfectly reasonable that any rational person will be apprehensive about spending such a large amount of money and question whether it is wise.

When it comes to this experience, my advice is this: Don’t dwell on it; if you possibly can, say to yourself ‘never mind the cost’, and just do it. Whether this is your first time in a helicopter or you have flown in one many times before, you are in for an amazing time and you will not regret it.

Review Title: Une vue du Grand Canyon incroyable
Review Text:
A une minute de notre hôtel à Tusayan, nous avons donc survolé pendant 30 minutes le Grand Canyon par un temps superbe (c'est le seul aléas qui peut faire basculer cette expérience).
Nous avons "perdu" 20 minutes de vol avant d'arriver au-dessus du Grand Canyon proprement dit mais l'attente valait le coup. Durée du vol complète: +/- 45/50 minutes.
La vue du Grand Canyon depuis un hélico n'a rien à voir avec celle que l'on peut avoir depuis les différents points de vue dans le parc. Et nous les avons tous faits !
C'est un très très grand moment tant pour nous que pour nos trois enfants. Ceux-ci étaient assis à côté du pilote avec une vue saisissante.
Nous étions derrière avec une vue très bonne aussi.
L'hélicoptère est très bon (Eurocopter, cocorico c'est européen !) et le pilote (Brett) était impeccable. Très professionnel, il a distillé ses commentaires à bon escient et a répondu à toutes les questions avec beaucoup de gentillesse. Attention, il ne parle qu'anglais. Pour les enfants ce fut donc un peu difficile. Mais le spectacle se passe de commentaires.
Le prix: c'est cher (1.370 $ pour 5) mais c'est une petite folie qu'on doit s'offrir.
A la fin du vol, la traditionnelle photo et le dvd du vol sont bien sûr payants (50 $ pour les deux) mais encore une fois c'est une très belle expérience et nous avons pris le "combo" photo/dvd.
Ils proposent aussi, à l'américaine, tout un tas de t-shirt, casquettes et produits dérivés en tout genre.
A noter le grand professionnalisme de tous les intervenants dans cette compagnie. Nickel !

We were shown a safety video before meeting our pilot and having photos taken, then boarding the helicopter.
I am not too good with heights and found myself seated in the front next to the pilot! Ryan was extremely competent and knowledgeable putting me at ease immediately. It was great to start In the front but we were also happy to switch with the other party in the back when we made a quick stop to refuel. Ryan's commentary was informative and interesting and he was more than happy to answer any questions put to him. Not sure if the soundtrack/playlist was provided by the company or the pilot, but we all really enjoyed that too.

Review Text:
The helicopter takes seven passengers, three in the front, four in the book. A computer algorithm assigns passengers to seats based on weight. If you show up obese, you will definitely be in the back row with a less expansive view than if you are in front. Overweight in the back please. Based on my observation, the charming pilots run their own algorithm which always, purely by chance, places the most attractive young lady in your group in the seat next to them.

My wife and I were teamed up with a family of four and we were both sent to the back of the bus. This seemed unfair but we are now determined to lose the weight necessary to be promoted to the front row next time.

Another slight problem is that you wear a headset throughout the flight and may have to listen to others in your party chit-chatting in a foreign language throughout the flight...slightly annoying.

Our pilot was both professional and pleasant. You will receive a pitch about the cost of flight school....and tips are therefore expected and gratefully accepted.

But even if you are in the second row and paired up with non-English speakers,this is a great experience. A tour of the GC is simply not complete without the helicopter ride.

Review Text:
There are 3 Helicopter companies operating flights out of the Grand Canyon airport. We had researched the alternatives and saw that there are essentially two flight paths that they all use. The short flight is 10 / 15minute across the forest and then up the western end of the Grand Canyon Park section of the canyon, and the longer 40 / 50 minute flight heads out east to the far end of the canyon then back along the canyon before returning to the airport along the route used by the shorter flight. We made our choice of company based upon the helicopters used and price. Maverick use the Eco-Star helicopters which have 7 passenger seats, all forward facing, in a cabin with big wrap around glass windows. The longer flight is only $30 more than the short flight at $249 + fees and taxes ($274 in total) but there is probably 10 times as much time spent flying over the canyon itself.
Brenton, our pilot, was brilliant. The flight starts off with a low flight over the Ponderosa Pine forest and then the forest suddenly vanishes from below you as you launch out over the canyon with the vertical drop of the chasm below you. Everyone on our flight gave an instant cheer as we suddenly encountered the thrill of the flight.
Yes, the cost is significant...but how often are you going to visit the Grand Canyon? We will remember the experience forever!

Review Title: Mit Fensterplatz fantastisch; hinten in der Mitte: spart das Geld!
Review Text:
Personal und Pilot sind sehr freundlich, nett und professionell. Wir haben einen Abend vorher die "Canyon Spirit Tour" vor Ort gebucht und wurden sehr freundlich über alles informiert. Bei uns zwei Personen wurde ein Fensterplatz garantiert, den wir auch bekommen haben.
Der Helicopter hat vorne vier Plätze (1 für den Piloten :-) ) und hinten 4 erhöhte Sitzplätze. Die Fensterplätze sind ohne Frage prima. Somit bekommt alles von einer Person die Bewertung ausgezeichnet. Der Pilot hat informativ erzählt, alle Fragen beantwortet und ist die Maschine sehr umsichtig geflogen.
Wer allerdings hinten die zwei Plätze in der Mitte nehmen muss (keine Wahl, da die Plätze nach Gewicht verteilt werden), kann sein Geld lieber sparen! Die Leute am Fenster verdecken mit ihren Armen beim fotografieren jede Sichtmöglichkeit. Auch nach vorne hin verdecken entweder die Köpfe die Sicht oder die Fensterstreben schränken das Blickfeld ein. Wer fotografieren möchte, hat überhaupt keine Chance, da die rechte hintere Scheibe auch noch stark zerkratzt war. Wir fühlen uns für den einen Betrag von 250 $ schlichtweg betrogen.
Dass das Fliegen und das Erlebnis an sich fantastisch ist, versteht sich von selbst.
Wir würden es aber nur empfehlen mit einem garantierten Fensterplatz!!
Kommt nicht in Versuchung, die DVD anschließend zu kaufen! Die DVD vom Flug ist überflüssig und blanke Abzocke. Der überdimensionale Weitwinkel verzerrt die Wirklichkeit. Die Farben sind dürftig bis mangelhaft bzw. nicht vorhanden, und die Aufnahme ist sehr pixelig.

Review Text:
I had planned my trip to vegas within an inch of my life. I had taken my partner for her birthday and this was her first visit to the USA I had planned concerts,shows,hot air balloon rides,buying an engagement ring from Tiffany and ultimately a trip to the Grand Canyon to ask a very special lady a very big question !
I chose maverick not because they were the cheapest, because they are not that, but because of their professional approach, the standard of aircraft, their fantastic safety record and they are the ONLY company that actually land inside the Grand Canyon
Our first flight was canceled due to high winds, we expected this as we had been at the pool that day and it sure was windy that day
Our second trip the next day was also canceled due to high winds, again we were expecting it because lying round the pool in 40* temperatures a strong breeze is very welcome and we fully understand that it's not great for helicopters flying around a canyon
Third time lucky we were greater by our pilot taken outside given a good safety briefing and off we go the trip was fantastic the narration funny but very informative from our enchanting pilot
The landing into the canyon smooth and without a hitch. The pilot then gets out some
Asti Spumante ............ Point of note to all American tour companies this is NOT champagne,not even close ! And a small plastic carton of a couple of grapes,slice of celery, a small carrot
I wish they hadn't bothered, it's the only let down to the whole experience. They let themselves and their clients down with this
However Maverick helicopter tours of Las Vegas I would fly with again I would recommend anyone who might be nervous to pay the extra dollars and go with the company that would rather cancel your trip than take you up when it's not safe it was a truly fantastic flight with a breathtakingly beautiful flight down the strip at night on the way back to the terminal
Our next planned trip is to Hawaii where maverick are in the process of setting up a new operation and we will definitely do the Islands tour with them there
Thank you to all that made our trip very magical
Sincere thanks Stephen & Jan Milton Keynes England

Review Title: The best thing I have EVER done
Review Text: My partner bought me this experience for my birthday as part of our USA road trip and it is quite literally the best thing I've ever done. The Maverick team were so friendly and professional and our pilot, Brett, made every effort to make our trip special, chatting to us, telling us anecdotes and explaining what we were seeing. There were some kiddies on our flight and he was great with them too. When you arrive they will take your photo with the helicopter, which you can buy (the photo not the helicopter) but we were also allowed to take our own photos with Brett after the flight so chose to give him a bigger tip instead of buying the photo. The flight itself was incredible - when we first flew over the rim into the canyon I burst in to tears - it was just the most beautiful, breathtaking sight ever.  The windows are really clean so you can take decent photos. We spent loads of time in the canyon and flew right across to the North Rim and back (although we were lucky as it's not always possible to get over there, depending on the weather). In total we were up for around an hour. A couple of things - (1) yes, seating is allocated by weight so you might not get a front or window seat. I was lucky, I had the front/side window, but my partner was at back/side window and he said it was still great. (2) sometimes the weather makes it unsafe to fly. Maverick cannot be held responsible for the weather! If you're undecided about making this trip DO IT, DO IT, DO IT! And I would definitively recommend Maverick as the people to fly with.

Review Title: The best way to see the Grand Canyon !

Review Text:
Hicimos esta excursion en la mañana (ellos nos recomendaron este horario proque se ve mejor el cañon).
La verdad que teniamos un poco de miedo cuando contratamos la excursion, pero finalmente no nos dio absolutamente nada de miedo ni vertigo.
Los helicopteros son super modernos (tienen costo de entre 2 y 3 millones de dolares), tienen una capacidad de 8 personas y cuando haces el check in en el aeropuerto (hay uo para Maverick y otro para Papillion) te pesan y la computadora automaticamente te asigna el mejor lugar dentro del helicoptero de acuerdo a tu peso. Antes de sentarte te dan las instrucciones de seguridad que son minimas. Al sentarte te colocan auriculares y todos los pasajeros, incluido el piloto, quedan comunicados entre si y se pueden hacer comentarios. El piloto que nos toco, Brent, super macanudo nos relato paso a paso todos los detalles del cañon.
Lo unico es que es todo en ingles; el piloto solo habla este idioma. Pero si no hablas ingles, igualmente el paseo vale la pena!!! Se los super recomiendo!
El paseo tiene una duracion de unos 50 minutos.

Maverick est une compagnie sérieuse et très bien organisée. Nous avons très peu attendu et nous avons été très bien accueilli.
Le skywalk be vaut pas le coup par contre car le situation de la passerelle n'est pas intéressante et n'offre pas un panorama terrible car on n'y voit pas le Colorado.
Il fait bien étudier les formules car certaines sont chères et comprennent des choses inutiles. Mon conseil aller a l'essentiel en prenant juste le tour en hélicoptère.

Review Title: Almost no views from rear 4 seats - no seating option
Review Text:
FAIR WARNING!!!!!!!!

Very disappointing!! Please note: THERE ARE 8 SEATS ON THE HELICOPTER, 1 FOR THE PILOT. IF YOU DON"T GET ONE OF THE REMAINING 3 FRONT SEATS, YOU WILL NOT SEE MUCH.

You have no choice in seating. The rear seats are advertised as 'stadium seating'. I am 6'3" and could not see over the people's heads in the front seats. I could see out one side, only. My wife was put in a middle rear seat, and could see even less.

Don't waster your money, unless you are a gambler willing to take a chance on getting a seat with decent visibility.

THERE IS NO WAY THIS TRIP IS WORTH $500+ dollars to get occasional glimpses of the Grand Canyon.

Review Text:
For our annual holiday my boyfriend and I went to Las Vegas with the intention of visiting the Grand Canyon. We had looked at various options and we eventually decided on visiting by doing something we've never done, that is to visit by helicopter.

We had booked the tour through our hotel and had decided on the Grand Canyon West Tour - Tribal Spirit. If you go on to their website and look for this tour you'll be able to get a more detailed breakdown of what the tour entails.

The plane ride to the Canyon was amazing and equally amazing was the helicopter ride into the Canyon itself. It really is difficult to get a perspective of how massive the Canyon is but going in by helicopter makes you see just why it's so impressive. We got to spend about 20 minutes in the Canyon which really is just enough time to take a few pictures. It's worth noting that when we transferred from the plane to the helicopter we had to wait around 20 minutes for the helicopter to arrive from Las Vegas as it had left after the plane.

After the helicopter into the Canyon you can take the shuttle bus to three different areas; Guano Point, Eagle Point (where the Skywalk is) and Hualapai Indian Village. The tour gives you only 1.5 hours to do all three of the sites. The shuttle is a bit hit and miss. When we went it was very busy owing to the government shut down making it a 30 minute wait for the shuttle bus so we went straight to Guano Point for some amazing views. The tour was included a lunch voucher for the cafe that is at Guano Point but you really don't have time for it and we didn't use it. We spent 15 minutes there before having to get on the shuttle back to the plane. There was another couple with us who had bought the Skywalk tour with the package to save time but they were unable to use it either.

Even with it not being busy I would say that 1.5 hours is not enough time to enjoy both Guano Point and Eagle Point with the Skywalk when you factor in the travel times. You've paid a lot of money of money for the tour to enjoy the view and take it all in but found most of my time seeing it behind the lens of my camera just to make sure I had something to remember it by. With the time available you have to decide on doing Guano Point or the Skywalk at Eagle Point and not both. If you've done the helicopter ride into the Canyon itself then I wouldn't bother with the Skywalk and just go straight to Guano Point, unless you really like the idea of seeing the Canyon right under your feet. If you are intending to do the Skywalk then purchase your ticket through Maverick Helicopters as it will save time queuing when you're there.

I did mention to the pilot on our return that there was not enough time to get lunch at Guano Point, but there was no offer of refunding or telling us to ask when we got back to the airfield for a refund. It's a use it or loose it. Not good enough. I would advise taking a sandwich or something as it's a long time without food and the pick up from the hotel is 06:30am.

All in all I felt that the company should be more realistic about the time you will actually have to enjoy the views. The tours look like you get to do lots of things but you don't. Prioritise what you want to do.

I'm glad we did it though!

Review Text: Several friends from England recommended that we take this helicopter tour if we were going to visit the Grand Canyon, and we are sure glad we did. Review Title: Outstanding experience with Maverick, and one piece of information to know
Review Text:
Apologies for the lateness of this review, but I was reviewing photos for a family Christmas letter and realized I had not posted a comment following our May 2013 helicopter tour of the Grand Canyon. Our helicopter tour was the absolute highlight of our Grand Canyon vacation this past summer. Read and believe all the 5-star ratings. We enjoyed it so much, that we did it twice in this vacation. The Maverick people, facility and helicopters are all top notch.

The one bit of information I wanted to share that I haven't seen posted elsewhere concerns seating arrangements in the helicopters. We flew in the EcoStar helicopters which have two rows of four-abreast seating. Prior to your flight, you will be weighed and this will feed into a weight-and-balance calculation that defines where you will be seated in the helicopter. (All aircraft deal with weight-and-balance, particularly small planes and helicopters.) The point is, you do not choose your seats. You could be seated behind a larger person and have a somewhat less expansive view. Obviously the front seat passengers have the best view. I rode in the front seat and loved it. I also rode in a rear side seat and loved it. I didn't experience a rear center seat. So my comments are just to alert you to the seating possibilities and implications.

While we flew with Maverick (and would again in a heartbeat), I expect the same weight-and-balance considerations and seating decisions would apply to all the tour providers.

I hope you choose to do a helicopter tour of the Canyon, and that your experience is as fun as ours.

Review Text:
Ok, let me say right off the bat I simply do not understand people who are afraid or hesitant to fly in a copter. After all, the Army used to pay me to jump out of them. Even riding in an open door with my feet on the skids never brought fear out in me. So the chance to fly in a $3 million Eco-Star over the most beautiful (and elusive for us) national treasure was a no-brainer. The closing of the federal government – and all the National parks – meant that the only way we were going to see this wonder is from the air. Thank heavens the tea-bagger congressmen had not restricted air space.

Arriving at the heliport, Hubby and I encountered very nice staff who took our weight in a most confidential fashion. Point: One must load a helicopter evenly or the thing either won’t get off the ground, or will be very hard to fly straight. Our pilot introduced himself, posed for photos and loaded us up after a safety briefing. As I had lost a great deal of weight this year, I was pleased to find myself with the window seat. Take off as smooth and easy as can be – and off we set. And my! What a view. I had to MAKE myself put the Nikon down to just gaze out the windows. We all had headsets and listened as our pilot pointed out landmarks. Less than an hour later, it was time to return to earth and our Detours guide, Chad.

Very unusual for me, I readily bought the photo with the pilot and also sprang for the video of our flight. Both very reasonably priced and quite good. Be prepared to pay a fuel surcharge of $15 per person. I do wonder though, if the fuel is getting more expensive or tourists are getting heavier?

Great experience – well worth the money!

Review Title: Waste of money for the people that get the back seats
Review Text:
The way the helicopter is set up is that there are 3 passenger seats in the front 4 and four in the back - everyone pays the same price. If you are one of the lucky ones in the front (seats determined by weight balance), then the $250+ price tag is completely worth it. I saw nothing from the front window (seats are too high), and the side window (at least I got a window seat... two people were not next to any window) was small. Plus, the pilot did not turn the helicopter 360 degrees, so I only saw the right side of things (meaning I missed half the tour).

On top of all this, the pilot we had was not good. He spent the majority of the time talking to the girl next to him and played music very loudly, so if you had any questions or concerns, they were not heard during the duration of the flight.

I've been on great helicopter tours before, so I know that it doesn't have to be this way. Save yourself the money.

Review Text:
Didn't want to do the Grand Canyon at all but figured...if I'm gonna do it, I may as well do it right.

We did the hour long tour and it was brilliant.

I've been in helicopters before - in London, and over Iguazu Falls in Brazil, and this Grand Canyon trip completely smashed the other two. There were five or six of us in the helicopter plus the pilot, and we flew very low at first, which puzzled me. Then I realised. As the pilot asked 'are you ready', and we flew over the edge, everyone let out a gasp and a 'oh my god'! I can't explain to you the feeling that I felt. It was humbling, awesome, a mixture of terror and complete unadulterated surprise and ecstasy. I've never felt like that before in my life. Truly once-in-a-lifetime. Great feeling, amazing views.

If you're reading this thinking 'but I couldn't fly in a helicopter, it's too scary' - it's actually surprising how little you feel it move. It's smooth, and it's a great feeling, so if you're considering doing it at the GC you should definitely just go for it.

I would give this six stars if I could. Thank you Maverick for such an awesome flight.

[It seems expensive but in comparison to other flights I've done it's actually really good value for the time you get and for the sheer raw emotion you'll feel.]

Review Text: We chose Maverick Helicopters because of reviews I'd read on Trip Advisor.  We flew from Tusayan, the town outside the park so we just went to the local airport which we could have walked to while staying at the Best Western.  I thought they were extremely professional, great helicopters, very solid and in great shape, with large windows so everyone gets a great view.  The waiting room was also very nice which was great because we waited a while to get on the flight but that's not a big deal.  My brother has flown helicopters for over 30 years and told me never to fly with anyone who wasn't Navy trained.  I laugh because it's not like I could check their credentials.  But there's a certain way of flying that I've noticed when with my brother that is hard to put into words.  They have a certain way of controlling the helicopter and of being aware of everything around them.  I have to say that I felt that certain something from Maverick, even though the pilot looked like he just graduated high school (he was a bit annoyed when I asked him where he trained but I promised my brother I would always do that, not that I could change anything at that point).  We took our flight in March and it was a bit misty in the canyon, so I can't say it was a breathtaking view, it really wasn't, but it was pretty amazing anyway. It was a treat to see the north side of the Grand Canyon, too.  When I returned home to tell my brother I'd flown with Maverick, his first response was "at least you chose a good company".  (whew!).  I would go with Maverick again if I make it back to the Grand Canyon mostly because they seem to be a first class operation that maintains their helicopters and you really want that when you're flying.

Review Title: Maverick helicopter tour was the highlight of our trip to Las Vegas
Review Text: I'm surprised by some of the negative comments about this tour on Tripadvisor - we had a fantastic trip and it was the highlight of our holiday to Las Vegas.  The helicopter is expensive but we thought well worth it - and there are other cheaper ways of seeing the canyon if you are on a budget.  Maverick pick you up from your hotel (by mini-bus, rather than the advertised limo) and take you to their helicopter terminal at the airport.  You get to ride in a small helicopter (maximum 7 passengers plus the pilot, atlhough our trip only had 6 passengers) and get excellent views.  Our pilot swapped us around so we all got a chance to sit in the front.  On the way to the canyon we flew over Hoover Dam, Lake Mead and Boulder City - the views were spectacular and at times the helicopter takes you along the course of the Colorado river within the walls of the canyon.  You stop at a spot within the canyon and have their "champagne breakfast" - or rather, more accurately, sparkling white wine and cheese and fruit - and from the picnic spot there are amazing views.  On the way back we flew by the Valley of Fire - an amazing outcrop of fire red rocks to the NE of Las Vegas.  Our pilot did give us a commentary and a music sound track (including "Come fly with me" and the "Ride of the Valkyries"!).  I got the impression Maverick work the pilots quite hard and don't pay them a great deal - from what our pilot said - but this is a very efficient operation and an amazing way to see one of the great natural wonders of the world.

Review Title: Helicopter view of Grand Canyon absolutely fantastic
Review Text:
Having read some of the reviews, we were not sure whether to splash out on a helicopter tour for three of us, but we're so glad we did. We booked a 25 minute ride with Maverick, from the little airport south of Tuseyan near the Canyon's South Rim. We got there half an hour early. The terminal building is bright, clean and very efficient. We checked in and were weighed (no, they don't tell you how much you weigh - you just stand on a plate and nobody is any the wiser!). We then waited til we were called by the pilot. Ours was called Cory and not only was he the most handsome pilot there, he was also a really great tour guide.

We had a thorough safety briefing and were then seated according to the plan they have, which I guess is based on the weight of each passenger to better balance the aircraft. We donned life jackets (as we fly over the Colorado River, it's a legal requirement), our safety belts, our head phones and microphones, and then we were off. First, we flew over the ponderosa forest toward the canyon. My husband and I hate heights but we were absolutely fine. My son and I were in the front and the helicopter was the type that meant we could see right down to the floor all round - great visibility. Even in the back, the seats are higher than the front to aid visibility. We spent about five minutes getting to the canyon and then we flew right over it. Oh, what an amazing view! We flew around the canyon for 15-20 minutes, over to the north rim, right over the Colorado river which looked like a stream below but which was 350 feet wide. We could see the rapids. Cory, the pilot, gave us great information and we were all able to ask questions - we could all hear through the headphones what everyone was saying. He clearly has a love for the Canyon and was a really interesting guide. He named the various peaks, talked about wildlife, pointed out the nearby
San Francisco mountain peaks, etc. We were very happy with the time we were over the Canyon - we'd feared we'd only fly over for 5 mnutes but we saw such alot. We all agreed it was one of, if not THE, best experiences of our lives. It cost quite alot but it was absolutely worth it. If you think the view from the Rim is incredible, just fly over it - you'll be stunned.

Too bad as the sunset tour is the most expensive tour and  for alot of folks this was a once in a lifetime trip.  On the way back, we had to stop, get out of the helicopter for him to get more fuel.  I felt this was a waste and would have preferred seeing a little more of the Grand Canyon. I would say you get what you pay for, but for 2 of us it was $1000.00 for less than 3 hrs. I would recommend a tour that has a  audio tape to listen to as you are flying- you will get more info than we did.
